about: Sidecar of finish-powerball-ultimate.json. The parameter-file format (spotless.params) carries values, units and a provenance note only, so the dose, the ranges, the values the registry's bounds cannot hold and the comparison with type D are here. Evidence and tags: docs/research/detergent-finish-ultimate.md. Not read by any code.

product.name: Finish Ultimate All in 1 (sold as Finish Powerball Ultimate All in One), United Kingdom
product.form: multi-compartment water-soluble capsule (powder, gel, liquid) in polyvinyl alcohol film
safetyDataSheets: D8395627 v2.0, formulation FF3233992, "Finish Powerball Ultimate All in 1", Switzerland, 16/12/2022: sodium carbonate 10 to 25 %, C12-14 alcohol EO/PO 10 to 25 %, percarbonate 10 to <25 %, etidronate up to 10 %, subtilisin <1 %, pH 9.4 to 10.4 at 10 %

D8408447, formulation FF3289622, "Finish Ultimate Dishwashing Tablets Fresh", Australia/New Zealand, 17/05/2024: sodium carbonate 10 to 30 %, C12-14 alcohol EO/PO 10 to <25 %, percarbonate 10 to <25 %, pH 9.4 to 10.4 at 10 %

D8411614, formulation FF3314399, "Finish Ultimate Dishwashing Tablets Lemon", Australia/New Zealand, 05/12/2025: sodium carbonate 30 to 60 %, C12-14 alcohol EO/PO 10 to <25 %, percarbonate up to 10 %, pH 10.4 to 11 at 10 %
product.safetyDataSheetsNote: No sheet for the United Kingdom was found. The three sheets do not agree; which of them the UK product of 2026 follows is not known. The best estimates (carbonate 30 %, percarbonate 10 %) sit where their bands meet.

dose.how: Sainsbury's unit prices on 2026-10-10: x55 at 13.75 GBP and 19.38 GBP/kg, x75 at 16.00 and 16.54, x32 at 9.00 and 21.80, each 12.90 g per unit. Pack weights 412.8 g for 32, 709.5 g for 55 and 967.5 g for 75 read on trolley.co.uk (a price aggregator) give the same 12.90 g; Tesco titles (search results only) add 1186.8 g for 92 and 1483.5 g for 115. The film is taken to be part of the declared weight. The range is an assumed fill tolerance of 1.5 %, not a sourced figure.

liq.xCarbonate.how: pH-equivalent value for 30 % soda ash, 10 % percarbonate, 2.5 % bicarbonate: stoichiometric carbonate 3.77 mol/kg (2.83 + 0.64 + 0.30), alkalinity 7.23 eq/kg plus about 0.1 from etidronate. The model has no bicarbonate term; 3.3 gives a main-wash pH 0.03 above that balance with the etidronate and 0.06 above it without (the exact equivalents are 3.0 and 2.6; the pH is flat in this parameter). Lower bound: the registry minimum. The 2022 and 2024 sheets (carbonate at most 25 to 30 %, pH 9.4 to 10.4 at 10 %) correspond to equivalents of 1.4 to 2.6, partly below what the registry allows.

liq.xSilicate.how: No silicate in the UK ingredient list. The upper bound stands for tetrasodium etidronate acting as a base.

liq.xPeroxide.how: Sodium percarbonate 10 % (6 to 16 %), 3 mol H2O2 per 314.0 g. 10 % is the only value inside the bands of all three sheets (up to 10 %; 10 to <25 % twice).

liq.xTaed.how: TAED 4 % (2.5 to 6 %), 228.25 g/mol: listed after percarbonate and before etidronate, the sulfonated polymer and the film.

liq.xProtease.unit: kg/kg (granulate of the type D grade)
liq.xProtease.how: No source gives a level or a grade (the 2022 sheet says only subtilisin <1 % as enzyme substance). The best value is a guess: 1.6 times the protease that 20 g of type D gives per wash. Lower bound: half the best value, 0.8 times type D per wash (parity per wash would be 0.0155). Upper bound: the registry maximum, 3.2 times type D per wash.

liq.xAmylase.unit: kg/kg (granulate of the type D grade)
liq.xAmylase.how: About half the protease, as in type D and in the Reckitt example of US 8,962,543 (0.8 and 0.4 %).

liq.xSurfactant.how: C12-14 alcohol ethoxylated propoxylated (PPG-5-laureth-5) 10 to <25 % in both Australian sheets and 10 to 25 % in the Swiss sheet of the exact product. The registry maximum is 0.1, so the file holds 0.1; the model uses the surfactant only for the liquor class, which is D either way.

liq.tabletTau.how: Film lag 60 s and contents 180 s at 40 C (chemistry 10.3, pouch column) expressed as one shrinking-core time that gives the same time to 90 % released.

liq.amylaseKox.how: The dossier's oxidation-stable amylase column (chemistry 10.5). The grade in the product is not disclosed; Reckitt's patent example names Stainzyme 12GT.

liq.tabletEa.why: A film dissolves with a steeper temperature dependence than a tablet (chemistry 10.3 gives 60 kJ/mol for the film), but no opened source gives a number and the time to release changes by under two minutes.

liq.proteaseHalfLife.why: The protease grade is not disclosed. If it is a heat-stable grade, 3600 s raises the mean protease of the main wash by 29 %.

liq.rinseAidDensity.why: Sister sheet D8411055 gives 1.01 to 1.02 g/cm3; a 1 to 2 % difference, recorded only.

notInTheModel: Manganese bleach catalyst (MN-TACN in the ingredient list): bleaches tea with hydrogen peroxide without TAED. The model's tea bleaching reads peracid and perhydroxyl only.
Acid from TAED (two acetyl groups per mole): lowers the main-wash pH by about 0.12 for this product, 0.05 for type D.
Staged release: powder, gel and liquid compartments dissolve at their own rates; the model releases every species in proportion to one dissolved mass.
Citrate, etidronate and polymers (hardness control), benzotriazole and the glass-care polymer.

predictedMainWash.conditions: First bath of auto_145 on the Bosch SMV4HAX40G: 4.0 L, dose released 60 s after circulation starts, heated from 19 to 64 C in about 19 min and held (temperature trace of packages/calibration/anchors/reports/first-build-demonstration.auto_145.md), 62.5 min. Computed with packages/sim-liquor on 2026-10-10; no soil in the liquor.

finish_ranges.note: Ranges of the model output over the parameter ranges above. The lower pH bound is the registry minimum of liq.xCarbonate; the older sheets suggest the real pH may be lower still (about 10.0 to 10.1 at 47 C).

factCheck.recomputedWith: own script against packages/sim-liquor; every figure of predictedMainWash reproduced
